content.title: About
content.content: Mock chicken legs are a plant‑based chicken substitute made from soy protein, wheat gluten and natural flavorings that mimic the taste and texture of real chicken drumsticks. The product is suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking to reduce meat consumption while keeping familiar flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mock chicken legs are often used in vegan versions of classic dishes such as BBQ wings or chicken nuggets.
The fibrous texture is created by high‑pressure extrusion of protein, producing meat‑like strands.
Flavor is enhanced with plant‑based chicken broth extracts and a blend of spices.
The product can be fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to offset nutrients lost when eliminating meat.
Many fast‑food chains offer mock chicken legs as a more sustainable menu option.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A serving provides about 15–20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with real chicken legs, it contains minimal saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Fortified iron helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels, especially in vegetarian diets.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat gluten adds a modest amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: The product contains no cholesterol, making it safe for those monitoring lipid levels.

items.title: Soy and gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains soy protein and wheat gluten, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for flavor; people watching sodium intake should monitor portion size.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: As with most meat analogues, it undergoes extensive processing, which may not suit those preferring whole foods.

items.title: Not gluten‑free
items.content: Because wheat gluten is a key ingredient, it is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mock chicken legs can be fried, baked, grilled, or roasted. They are often marinated in soy sauce, spices and oil, then coated in breadcrumbs for a crispy crust. Serve with BBQ, honey‑mustard, or spicy sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it lasts 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze up to 3 months, packing tightly to minimize air.
